thread:
samir: Heads-up: eu-west1 batch attach latency jumped, provisioning queue stalled. Seeing attach timeouts and nodes entering drain.

tay: Any storage logs to correlate? high-level symptom sounds like IO saturation or device errors.

samir: quick kernel excerpt from gnode-ew1-72:

[ 2100.123456] nvme0: completed async event fatal_error (00)
[ 2100.123789] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 4096
[ 2100.124001] Buffer I/O error on dev nvme0n1p1, logical block 8192
[ 2100.124210] EXT4-fs (nvme0n1p1): Delayed block allocation failed for inode 54321: ret=-5

leah: hmm. Region had a cleaner burst at 04:10 UTC from adhoc-cron:cleaner-burst (concurrency=50) to clear a long backlog. That probably pushed ephemeral devices into write-amplification.

infra-ci: deploy/cleaner/2026-03-21T04:06 by ci-cd (sha: c3f9a2). Note: that cron job was triggered manually by ops-sched.

tay: If concurrency was 50 that's huge for tiny ephemeral NVMe. We should reduce concurrency and add hotspot-aware behavior.

samir: Mitigation options I want to try now (low-risk first):
1) throttle cleaner concurrency to 6 for eu-west1 canary shards
2) temporarily remap image staging dir to read-only overlay while we attach GPUs (reduces metadata writes)
3) reprovision nodes with >8 EIO events and mark them for firmware POST-health check
4) enable io cgroup write throttle for janitor cgroup while we drain backlog

leah: Commands: 
# set cleaner concurrency canary
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/cleaner CONCURRENCY=6 --record --selector=region=eu-west1-canary

# remap image staging to read-only overlay (one-liner for kube):
kubectl -n batch patch ds image-stager -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"volumes":[{"name":"staging-ro","hostPath":{"path":"/srv/staging-ro","type":"DirectoryOrCreate"}}]}}}}'

samir: For reprovisioning I'll run:
./tools/prov --region eu-west1 --filter "eio_events>=8" --action reprovision --batch 3

tay: Also propose quick telemetry change: emit iostat snapshot every 30s for devices with >200% baseline IOPS so we can detect flash hotspots automatically.

sre-oncall: I'll add a temporary alert: local-nvme-hotspot (threshold: 3 nodes with device iops >200% baseline for 3m). Creating now.

ops-bot: alert created: local-nvme-hotspot-eu-west1 at 3251111200 (rule: local-nvme-hotspot)

leah: Ran the canary concurrency change. Two canaries show IOPS drop ~35% and fewer write errors.

samir: Reprovision kicked off. First batch completed, node gnode-ew1-72 reprovisioned and passed attachment tests. GPUs attached cleanly.

tay: Good. We still have ~18k cleaner backlog; long-term fix: add adaptive concurrency + BPF-based write-shaper to keep janitor from saturating device queues. Filing ticket.

infra-ci: ticket INFRA-8421 created: "adaptive-cleaner-concurrency + io-shaping" (owner: tay)

sre-oncall: I'll draft runbook steps: detection, safe throttle commands, reprovision flow, and cost tradeoffs (pause vs reprovision). ETA 3 hours.

ops-bot: alert resolved: local-nvme-hotspot-eu-west1 at 3251112350 (rule: local-nvme-hotspot)

samir: Region attach queue healthy again. Leaving thread open for an hour to watch.

leah: Note for postmortem: avoid adhoc bursts >20 concurrency on ephemeral pools; prefer staggered drains and targeted reclaims.

tay: Also schedule firmware health scans for nodes reprovisioned this week; possible vendor firmware bug on recent firmware bundle.

sre-oncall: Adding that to postmortem checklist and will include cost estimate for repeated reprovisions.

samir: Thanks team. Follow-up sync tomorrow if needed.
